name: Cloudflare Sandbox
oneLiner: A Worker that starts a Firecracker microVM, with no public port, no region pinning, and a disk that is wiped when the instance stops.
whatItIs: Cloudflare Sandboxes are a feature of the Workers platform: you write a Worker, its Durable Object starts a Linux container on Cloudflare's network, and that container runs untrusted or generated code with its own kernel.

There is no separate sandbox service to sign up for and no sandbox console. Identity is a Durable Object name, compute is a container instance, and persistence is a snapshot you take yourself or a bucket you mount.
A second, lighter environment called Dynamic Workers runs JavaScript, Python or WebAssembly inside the Workers runtime when the code only needs to call methods you pass in.
whoFor: Teams already running a Worker who want untrusted code execution next to their application, with the Worker holding the credentials and deciding reachability.
isolation: A Firecracker microVM per container, with its own kernel and network. Your image runs as a Linux container inside it, and every process has root capabilities, so there is no privilege boundary between users inside one sandbox. No memory snapshot, no pause, no fork. Docker-in-Docker works with iptables and IP forwarding off; `linux/amd64` only.
sizes: Six presets from `lite` (1/16 vCPU, 256 MiB, 2 GB) to `standard-4` (4 vCPU, 12 GiB, 20 GB). Custom sizes are capped at 4 vCPU / 12 GiB / 20 GB, with at least 3 GiB of memory per vCPU. No GPU and no ARM. Placement is chosen by Cloudflare near the request, and a sandbox cannot be pinned to a region.

billing.model: Per-10-millisecond Containers usage on the account's Workers Paid bill, plus Workers, Durable Objects, egress, R2 and optionally Logs.
billing.meter: Active CPU $0.072 per vCPU-hour, provisioned memory $0.009 per GiB-hour and provisioned disk $0.000252 per GB-hour while the instance runs. Egress is $0.025 per GB in North America and Europe.
billing.stopped: Nothing. A stopped instance is not billed, and its disk and processes are gone.
billing.planFee: Workers Paid has a $5 a month minimum for the account. There is no sandbox-specific plan or fee.
billing.minimum: No free tier for containers: the Free column is N/A for memory, CPU and disk. The plan includes about $0.73 of container usage a month.

well: A Worker that already holds the credentials and decides what the code can reach: the sandbox never gets a public port.
One microVM per user or per job, with no shared kernel, at a per-second price that reaches zero when it stops.
A team already on Cloudflare: one account, one bill, Workers and Durable Objects alongside.
A JavaScript or Python snippet that does not need a container at all: a Dynamic Worker starts faster.
badly: A long job with no inbound requests: code inside does not count as activity, so a two-hour build dies at the timeout.
Any workload needing more than 4 vCPU, 12 GiB or 20 GB, or a GPU.
EU data residency: a sandbox cannot be pinned to a region.
An agent that expects a pause or a resumable machine: stopping deletes the disk and every process.

usability.dashboard: A Cloudflare account dashboard for Workers, containers, instance IDs and logs. There is no sandbox console and no create-a-sandbox button.
usability.withoutCode: No. The first step is a Worker with a Durable Object, and the image build needs Docker locally.
usability.signup: A Cloudflare account and the Workers Paid plan at a $5 monthly minimum, which needs a payment method. No waitlist.
usability.docs: 121 sandbox pages, each with a Markdown twin, plus `llms.txt`. Support is the community portal, cases, chat or phone depending on plan; no response-time commitment is published for Workers Paid.
tripsUp: The 10-minute idle stop belongs to the deprecated 0.x SDK, not to Sandboxes 1.0.
Stopping the instance deletes the files on its disk.
The 2 vCPU / 4 GiB and 4 vCPU / 8 GiB shapes do not exist.
Sandbox names are routing keys, not authentication.
A deploy does not update a running sandbox.

caveats.issue: The 10-minute idle stop is 0.x behaviour, not the current product
caveats.detail: The legacy `Container` class and the 0.x SDK stop after 10 minutes by default. Sandboxes 1.0 has no default inactivity timeout, a 6-hour maximum, and stops shortly after the Durable Object goes inactive. The 0.x SDK gets fixes only until 31 December 2026.

evidence.quote: After a period of inactivity (10 minutes by default, configurable via `sleepAfter`), the container stops to free resources.
Without a timeout, Cloudflare stops the instance shortly after the Durable Object becomes inactive.

caveats.issue: Start time is milliseconds on the product page and 1–3 seconds in the docs
caveats.detail: The product page promises milliseconds; the Containers FAQ says a cold start is often 1–3 seconds depending on image size and execution time.

evidence.quote: Sandboxes start in milliseconds, not minutes.
Container cold starts can often be in the 1-3 second range, but this is dependent on image size and code execution time, among other factors.

caveats.issue: Outbound internet is off by default, required, or on by default depending on the page
caveats.detail: The sandbox security guide says `enableInternet: false` is the default; the API reference says the field is required when options are passed; the Containers guide says the other API allows internet by default. Treat egress as an explicit per-start decision.

evidence.quote: A Container starts with `enableInternet: false` by default, so it cannot reach the Internet.
By default, a Container will allow internet access

caveats.issue: Instance maximums are called defaults that can be increased, and a hard table
caveats.detail: The limits page says all maximums can be increased, directly above a custom-instance table that states 4 vCPU, 12 GiB and 20 GB as constraints. Whether support can lift them is not published.

evidence.quote: All instance size maximums and account limits on this page are defaults and can be increased.

caveats.issue: “Start building for free” does not include a free sandbox
caveats.detail: The product page invites you to start for free; the Containers rate card lists N/A for memory, CPU and disk on the Free plan, and the docs require Workers Paid.

caveats.issue: A sandbox cannot be pinned to a region
caveats.detail: Containers support region and jurisdiction constraints, but the `durable_object` policy that sandboxes use rejects placement constraints. Placement is chosen for latency and can change when an instance restarts.
Stopping the instance deletes the files on its disk. Only a snapshot (30 days, 20 GB maximum) or an R2 directory backup or mount survives it.

The Workers SLA covers Workers only, and no Containers or Sandboxes SLA page exists. The status page has no Sandboxes component, so an outage surfaces as a Workers, Durable Objects or Containers incident.

caveats.issue: Compliance scope for this product is unpublished
caveats.detail: Cloudflare holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS L1 and a HIPAA AoC company-wide. No public statement says the audit boundary includes Containers or Sandboxes, and the reports sit behind the dashboard.

strengths: A Firecracker microVM per sandbox with no public port; inbound is HTTP through your Worker only.
Active-CPU billing: a stopped instance costs nothing, and idle time bills memory and disk but no CPU.
One account and one bill alongside Workers, Durable Objects and R2.
Snapshots, R2 directory backups and S3/R2 mounts cover three different persistence needs.
A large, mature security programme behind the platform.
